rounds.text: Lloyds Metals & Energy Ltd is displaying explosive operational scaling, highlighted by iron ore production surging 120% in a single year from 10 million to 22 million tons [E83], alongside compounded sales growth reaching 230% over the trailing twelve months [E16]. This aggressive expansion is underpinned by stellar capital efficiency, evidenced by an extraordinary ROE of 36.6% [E13] and an ROA of 11.82% that comfortably outpaces the sector benchmark of 4.81% [E8]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is surging with positive money flow [E42] and foreign and domestic institutions expanding their respective holdings [E40, E41], all while a DCF model indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 3564 per share, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 46.2% [E43, E44]. Conceded: [E2] and [E37], showing that the heavy capital expenditure program has driven up borrowings to Rs 20,716 Cr [E37] and elevated the price-to-book ratio to 7.80x [E2]. Nevertheless, the company's second pellet plant has successfully commissioned to reach 8 million tons of capacity [E79], and management has guided for FY27 iron ore production to hit 26 million tons [E75] while targeting over Rs 2,000 crores in annual cost savings by March 2028 [E76].

evidence.quote: Our FY '27 guidance reflects the next change in our scale, iron ore production at 26 million tons, dispatches of 27 million tons, pellet of 7.75 million to 8 million tons, DRI at 825,000 tons and a formal entry into steelmaking with wire rod mill production at around 150,000 tons.

evidence.quote: We expect annual cost savings to surpass INR2,000 crores per annum as all logistics and sustainability initiatives are maturing by March '28.

evidence.fact: Management stated that steel markets and iron ore demand remain as strong as ever, particularly in the Indian market.
evidence.quote: The steel markets and therefore, iron ore are as strong as ever, especially in Indian market.

evidence.fact: The company has invested INR13,500 crores in capex over the last 4 years.
evidence.quote: Konsari, in Gadchiroli, we have completed the 2 pellet plants reaching capacity of 8 million tons, making us the largest merchant pellet player by far.

evidence.fact: The second pellet plant was commissioned in May 2026, taking total pellet capacity to 8 million tons per annum.
evidence.quote: I'm also pleased to share that the second pellet plant was commissioned in May 2026. This takes our total pellet capacity to 8 million tons per annum and positions us strongly for FY27 volume growth.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margin held steady at approximately 34% across the last two quarters.
evidence.quote: The EBITDA margin has held steady at approximately 34% across both the last 2 quarters, demonstrating structural cost efficiency and not one-off gains.

evidence.fact: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin stood at 33.77%, up 418 basis points year-on-year.
evidence.quote: EBITDA margin for the full year stood at 33.77%, up 418 basis points year-on-year.

evidence.fact: Logistics cost for most iron ore output is expected to reduce by more than INR500 a ton via the planned 195-kilometer pipeline.
evidence.quote: This pipeline will reduce logistic cost for most of the iron ore output by us by more than INR500 a ton and is in advanced planning stage.

evidence.fact: Iron ore production scaled from 10 million to 22 million tons, representing a 120% growth in a single year.
evidence.quote: On operations, our iron ore scaled from 10 million to 22 million tons, which is a 120% growth in a single year.

evidence.fact: The first pellet plant reached 100% capacity utilization within 4 months of commissioning.
evidence.quote: The pellet plant commissioned at the fag end of Q2 reached 100% capacity utilization within just 4 months, 3 million tons in 9 months, a ramp-up that very few plants anywhere in the country have achieved.

evidence.fact: Total pellet capacity stands at 8 million tons per annum following the commissioning of the second pellet plant.
evidence.quote: This takes our total pellet capacity to 8 million tons per annum and positions us strongly for FY27 volume growth.

evidence.fact: Standalone net debt as of March 31, 2026, stood at INR3,901 crores.
evidence.quote: Stand-alone net debt as on 31st March 2026 stands at INR3,901 crores, a manageable level given our EBITDA generation.

evidence.quote: We expect annual cost savings to surpass INR2,000 crores per annum as all logistics and sustainability initiatives are maturing by March '28.

evidence.quote: Along with this, we will be achieving 100,000 tons of copper over the next 3 to 5 years from both CHEMAF and Surya.
